cards.explanation: The answer is that the Jews there were trying to kill Him. John 7:1 says Jesus did not want to travel in Judea, "…because the Jews there were trying to kill Him." So He stays up in Galilee for now. I think that's one place where staying put is just plain wisdom, friends.

The answer is His disciples there. His brothers say, "Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing." (John 7:3) Those are the people they name. I think they sound like that friend who watches you do one good thing and yells, "Put it in the group chat! Tell EVERYBODY!" And here's the plot twist, friends: the very next verse says even His own brothers did not believe in Him. (John 7:5)

The answer is False. John 7:5 says, "For even His own brothers did not believe in Him." The word "even" says a lot there, friends. These are His own family, standing right in front of Him, giving Him advice.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come." (John 7:6) Their time is always at hand. His is not yet, friends. I think His brothers could walk out the door any time they pleased, and that's the difference He's pointing to.

The answer is that He testifies that its works are evil. That's the reason Jesus gives when He says, "The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil." (John 7:7) He tells the truth, and the world hates Him for it. His brothers don't get that treatment, and He says so.

The answer is not publicly but in secret. John 7:10 says that after His brothers had gone up, He also went, "not publicly, but in secret." So He told them He wasn't going, stayed behind, and then went up after them, quietly. The text doesn't say more about how He pulled it off, friends, so I'll leave that to the passage.

The answer is that He deceives the people. The text says some said, "He is a good man." But others replied, "No, He deceives the people." (John 7:12) Same crowd, same Jesus, two totally different opinions, friends. And they were whispering the whole time.

The answer is False. Many in the crowds were whispering about Him, and John 7:13 says, "Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews." So the talk stayed quiet, and fear of the Jews is the reason the text gives. Whispering at a feast, friends. That's a lot of quiet.
